newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo sees gold price upturn in due course.
newsitem.headline: Anglo sees gold price upturn in due course.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, the world's largest gold producer, said on Thursday it expected an eventual recovery in the gold price based on robust physical demand for the metal.
"There will be a turning (point) when gold will come back into favour," Kelvin Williams, marketing director, told reporters at a results presentation.

"We really see the gold market as being balanced on a robust gold offtake (and) satisfactory demand, passing through an evolutionary cycle of reconsideration by some players...it will continue to be a real and effective market for a very long and interesting time to come."
Williams said initial indications were that physical demand for gold in 1996 had matched the record levels seen in 1995.
Referring to market anxieties about central bank sales of gold, he said this was a real issue but would not lead to "Armageddon" in the gold market.
Gold would remain a reserve asset for central banks around the world and the current debate on the level of holdings would not persist forever.
"It is not something that will go on into the 2000s."
Low inflation had contributed to the slide in the gold price, which saw the yellow metal fall below $350 an ounce for the first time in more than three years on Wednesday.
"That cuts the ground from under gold and other commodities," he said.
